record.context_brief: Daróczy equation on the natural numbers
record.original_question: Determine whether every function φ:N→(0,∞) satisfying Daróczy's equation φ(n) = φ(n+1) + φ(n(n+1)) for all natural numbers n must be of the form φ(n) = c/n for some constant c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let N = {1, 2, 3, ...} denote the set of positive integers. Suppose φ : N → (0, ∞) is a function satisfying the functional equation
    φ(n) = φ(n + 1) + φ(n(n + 1))
for every n ∈ N. Decide whether every such function φ must have the form φ(n) = c/n for some positive constant c. Equivalently, classify all positive solutions of this equation.
artifact.category_tag: Functional equations in a single variable
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface any published resolution of Daróczy's problem asking whether every positive solution φ : N → (0,∞) of φ(n) = φ(n+1) + φ(n(n+1)) is of the form c/n. The problem is listed among open problems in recent surveys on functional equations in a single variable, and no proof or counterexample is found in the available literature.
